locations/detailed-world-map-seed.content:
Detailed World Map Seed
One-Line Summary
The Neon Champions map should be a layered 2052 world of ordinary geography distorted by White Sky maintenance, climate damage, corporate concessions, mineral corridors, compute/water/food infrastructure, migration pressure, and regions that disagree over whether survival under the pale sky is rescue or occupation.
Naming Rule
Avoid region names that sound like a writer trying to be cool.
Prefer names that could plausibly appear in:

treaties;
insurer maps;
shipping manifests;
migration paperwork;
climate litigation;
corporate concession contracts;
activist slogans;
military logistics;
local slang derived from real infrastructure.

Good generic forms:

Basin Security Area
Rainfall Compensation District
Albedo Impact Zone
Coastal Protection Authority
Hydrological Exception Zone
Climate Stabilization Concession
Bonded Cloud Zone
Model Freeport
Compute Concession
Port Continuity District
Receiver City
Work-Residency Zone
Carbon Custodial Territory
Solar Curtailment Province

These are intentionally bureaucratic. Cyberpunk is stronger when the horror arrives in paperwork.
Recommended White Sky Beneficiaries
Best Recommendation: High-Asset Temperate and Subtropical Corridors
The sincere defenders of White Sky should not be only villains. The strongest beneficiaries are high-asset regions that avoided catastrophic heat, crop, insurance, and infrastructure losses because the intervention bought time.
Likely defenders:

North Atlantic financial/insurance states and protected coastal metros.
Parts of Europe that avoided extreme heat mortality and infrastructure breakdown.
Wealthy Asian and Pacific coastal industrial corridors that need stable ports, fabs, and logistics.
Gulf / desert engineering states that reduced lethal heat while selling cooling, desalination, and climate services.
Corporate agriculture and food-logistics regions whose yields became insurable again.
Cities whose climate debt would otherwise have bankrupted them.

Important nuance: many ordinary people in these places sincerely believe White Sky saved their parents, crops, hospitals, and cities. They are not all corporate puppets.
Why This Works Scientifically
Albedo intervention plausibly reduces heat stress and some heat extremes. Places with capital, infrastructure, insurance, courts, and political leverage can convert that cooling into stability. They can also litigate, hedge, and compensate losses better than poor regions.
So the injustice is not simply “White Sky helps the north and hurts the south.” It is:

White Sky creates a global risk redistribution system, and the powerful are better at converting uncertainty into protection, liability shields, and profit.

Recommended White Sky Harm / Opposition Region
Best Recommendation: West Africa and the Sahel, Extending into the Gulf of Guinea
This is the strongest lower-income opposition center because it combines:

West African monsoon sensitivity;
Sahel heat and rainfall volatility;
farmer/pastoralist pressure;
Lake Chad hydrological politics;
coastal megacity flooding around Lagos and the Gulf of Guinea;
major youth population and migration politics;
solar potential affected by a brightened sky;
resource corridors tied to global battery/compute economies;
plausible climate-justice movements;
enough urban density and cultural power to avoid making it a passive victim zone.

This region can plausibly argue:

the sky was changed without consent;
rainfall timing shifted;
heat relief was used to justify debt and concessions;
seas still rose;
solar revenue was curtailed;
mineral extraction intensified;
compensation arrived as corporate control.

Scientific Logic
Use monsoon timing and attribution, not simple desertification.
A delayed or distorted monsoon is better fiction than “less rain everywhere”: farmers plant based on expected rain; seed fails; rains arrive late and flood; insurers call it natural variability; corporate climate models deny responsibility; activists call it atmospheric occupation.
The key conflict is not whether White Sky made Africa hotter. It may have cooled heat extremes. The conflict is whether cooling was bought by altering rainfall, solar, debt, food, and sovereignty.
Regional Subzones to Develop
Use real geography first, then local institutional names.
Western Sahel Rainfall Claims
Focus: Senegal/Mauritania/Mali/Burkina Faso/Niger-facing rainfall timing, grazing corridors, food security, security contractors, climate courts.
Conflict: farmers and pastoralists accuse sky operators of moving the rain line. Corporate defendants point to uncertainty and pre-existing vulnerability.
Possible institution names:

Western Sahel Rainfall Claims Board
Sahel Basin Security Areas
Rainfall Compensation Districts
Monsoon Variance Courts

Lake Chad Pulse Zone
Focus: Nigeria/Niger/Chad/Cameroon borderlands, mobile shorelines, fishing, grazing, armed groups, water models, humanitarian biometric systems.
Conflict: the lake is not simply gone; it pulses. Whoever controls the model controls aid, security, and settlement legitimacy.
Better name: Lake Chad Hydrological Exception Zone.
Lagos / Gulf of Guinea Floodline
Focus: Lagos, Accra, Abidjan, coastal informal settlements, ports, lagoons, insurance withdrawal, elite raised districts, sewage/flood disease, cable landings.
Conflict: White Sky propaganda says the world was saved; the sea still enters homes.
Possible institution names:

Gulf of Guinea Coastal Protection Authorities
Lagos Lagoon Receiver Districts
Port Continuity Corridors
Coastal Insurance Redlines

Niger Delta / Gulf Energy Transition Zone
Focus: old oil infrastructure, petrochemical ruins, gas, ports, militias, flood/salinity, cleanup debt, new battery/material logistics.
Conflict: fossil extraction history is converted into climate-stabilization debt logic. The same region harmed by old carbon is asked to host new climate-control infrastructure.
Possible institution names:

Niger Delta Remediation Concessions
Gulf Energy Transition Districts
Salinity Buffer Areas

Congo Basin Carbon and Mineral Custody
Focus: Congo Basin forests, peatlands, illegal roads, carbon finance, conservation drones, bioprospecting, copper/cobalt corridors, Kinshasa as data/legal center.
Conflict: the world wants the Congo to remain a carbon sink and a mineral supplier at the same time.
Possible institution names:

Congo Basin Carbon Custodial Territories
Cuvette Centrale Peat Security Areas
Copper-Cobalt Export Corridors
Kinshasa Data Entrepôt

Nile Attribution Corridor
Focus: Blue Nile / Nile Basin dam politics, hydropower, irrigation, rainfall attribution, Egypt/Sudan/Ethiopia diplomacy, food security.
Conflict: every bad water year becomes a White Sky accusation, a dam accusation, and a governance accusation.
Possible institution names:

Nile Basin Climate Attribution Tribunal
Blue Nile Hydropower Security Compact
Irrigation Guarantee Zones

Zambezi Load-Shed Corridor
Focus: Zambia/Zimbabwe/Mozambique/Southern Africa hydropower volatility, drought, grid failure, mines, cities, regional power pools.
Conflict: drought years become power politics; mines get electricity while neighborhoods get darkness.
Possible institution names:

Zambezi Power Allocation Areas
Hydropower Revenue Protection Zones
Southern Grid Emergency Compacts

Corporate Presence Pattern
Corporate regions are common worldwide, but not uniform.
Where They Are Largest

lower-income resource extraction centers;
climate-bankrupt cities;
port and cable chokepoints;
mineral rail corridors;
water/desalination systems;
datacenter/power basins;
biosecure clinic and agricultural zones;
migration work-residency towns;
White Sky maintenance sites.

Where They Are Smaller

rural service towns;
logistics depots;
company housing blocks;
clinics;
cooling shelters;
private security districts;
bonded cloud/data facilities;
seed/fertilizer distribution nodes.

Where They Are Weak or Absent
There should definitely be backwaters:

regions with low immediate resource value;
areas too risky to insure;
places with strong local resistance and weak service profitability;
remote interiors not needed for corridors;
territories where informal institutions work better than corporate contracts;
zones with Digital-Net contamination or bad data histories that make actuarial control unreliable.

Backwaters are useful. They stop the world from feeling completely paved over. They are where old cultures, outlaw clinics, unreliable archives, folk politics, small warlords, local Champions, and strange Digital-Net phenomena survive.
Corporate Archetypes Recommendation
Use all archetypes, but rank them by setting importance.
Tier 1: Most Central
Climate Migration Work-Towns
These are extremely cyberpunk and thematically strong.
Why: they connect climate, labor, housing, borders, medicine, body subscriptions, family separation, and corporate dependency in one institution.
Use them in Africa, South Asia, Gulf states, coastal megacities, agricultural regions, and reconstruction zones.
Debt-Receivership Cities
These are politically strong because they show corporate rule arriving through finance rather than invasion.
Why: elections remain, but budgets, cooling, policing, land sales, utility rates, and identity systems are administered by a receiver consortium.
Use them in flood-hit coastal cities, bankrupt industrial cities, and disaster-rebuilt metros.
Critical Minerals / Infrastructure Concessions
These are essential for lower-income cyberpunk themes.
Why: they explain how global climate salvation depends on extraction, security, rail, ports, and body-harming labor elsewhere.
Use them in DRC/Zambia, Indonesia, lithium triangle analogues, Arctic prospects, and African rail/port corridors.
Tier 2: Very Useful
Biosecure Health Zones
Strong for biotech, subscription bodies, fertility, pathogen politics, and mutation.
Port / Cable / Logistics Corridors
Strong for strategic map play, feed provenance, trade, and deniable wars.
Bonded Cloud / Compute Concessions
Useful, but explain carefully. See below.
Tier 3: Use Sparingly
Resilience Arcologies
Good visual anchor, but can become generic cyberpunk if overused. Best as elite districts inside larger cities, not entire-world default.
What Is a Compute Freeport?
The name is not necessarily bad, but it should mostly be an official category, not a colorful area name.
A compute freeport is a special legal/economic zone for computation, analogous to a customs freeport.
It may offer:

tax/customs exemptions for chips, cooling systems, batteries, reactors, satellite links;
special energy and water rights;
data-sovereignty carve-outs;
model-weight escrow under foreign or corporate law;
arbitration courts;
biometric worker housing;
private security;
sanctions gray zones;
climate-model hosting for White Sky operations;
VI allocation and inference quotas.

In-world reason: White Sky, insurance, finance, biotech, logistics, and military planning require massive trusted computation. Compute is treated like a strategic commodity, not just a service.
Better map labels:

Bonded Cloud Zone
Model Freeport
Compute Concession
Sovereign Cloud Concession
Data Entrepôt
Cloud Entrepôt
Exempt Compute District
Model Haven, as slang

Recommendation: use “compute freeport” in exposition as the generic institution, but name actual places after geography and legal function: e.g. Mombasa Sovereign Cloud Port, Kinshasa Data Entrepôt, Tema Bonded Cloud Zone, Zambezi Compute Concession.
Blue Week Direction
Blue Week should be a real event caused by eco-anarchist sabotage or atmospheric intervention against White Sky maintenance.
Core idea:
An eco-anarchist network concludes that corporate climate life-support has become a permanent hostage system. They do not simply want apocalypse. They believe the world must be forced to experience the sky as contingent, not owned.
They sabotage, spoof, or chemically disrupt part of the White Sky maintenance lattice. For several days, some regions see real blue sky.
The event is beautiful, terrifying, and morally indefensible all at once.
Important nuance: the eco-anarchists are not obviously right. If White Sky maintenance fails at scale, termination shock and heat rebound could kill millions. But they are also not cartoon villains: their critique of corporate atmospheric dependency is legitimate.
Possible group labels:

Blue Restorationists: broad movement, not necessarily violent.
Open Sky Cells: direct-action eco-anarchists.
Terminationists: derogatory label used by Sky Loyalists.
Unceiling networks: activist slang.
Atmospheric commons movement: legal/political wing.

Campaign Crisis Recommendation
Do not choose one world-ending crisis yet. Build the setting around a braided crisis:

Blue Week proves White Sky can be disrupted.
A West African monsoon/rainfall attribution case turns the disruption into global politics.
A debt-receivership city or port corridor becomes the immediate campaign map where corporate, state, Free-Net, and Champion forces collide.
A body-rights or labor uprising gives it human texture.

This is stronger than a single disaster because it lets the world reveal itself by layers.
Best seed sequence:

Blue Week occurs.
Sky Loyalists demand emergency powers to secure the maintenance lattice.
West African rainfall claimants argue the sabotage revealed hidden tuning records.
Corporate receivers move to protect ports, cloud zones, and migration work-towns.
Free-Net archivists leak contradictory climate-model fragments.
Champions become visible because institutions cannot resolve the crisis fast enough.

Open Questions

Is Blue Week centered in West Africa, global in patches, or first noticed through feed discrepancy?
Which city should become the first detailed map: Lagos, Kinshasa, Alexandria, Mombasa, Dakar, Accra, Cairo, Johannesburg, or a fictional composite?
Should the first campaign region include both coastal flood politics and inland rainfall politics?
Is the first White Sky corporation primarily climate/insurance, cloud/compute, chemicals/aerospace, agriculture, or a shell joining all of them?

locations/greenland.title: Greenland
locations/greenland.content:
Greenland
One-Line Summary
Greenland is the first strong candidate for Neon Champions’ initial campaign region: a sparse Arctic strategic theater where climate infrastructure, mineral concessions, sovereignty politics, data routes, fisheries, and White Sky control collide without becoming a conventional battlefield.
Canon Status
Soft-canon draft. The direction is strong, but the exact fictionalization level, campaign name, and White Sky node identity need user approval.
What It Is
Greenland remains recognizably Greenland / Kalaallit Nunaat: an autonomous Arctic territory with local sovereignty politics, Danish and allied defense entanglements, small but strategically huge settlements, and a landscape shaped by ice, sea, rock, weather, and distance.
By the campaign era, climate change has not made Greenland easy. It has made Greenland more accessible, more unstable, more valuable, and more exposed to outside money.
Why It Matters
Greenland sits at the crossing of:

Arctic shipping and search-and-rescue routes;
rare-earth and critical-mineral pressure;
fisheries and cold-chain logistics;
satellite, radar, and weather infrastructure;
White Sky polar calibration and atmospheric monitoring;
cold compute, hydro, and data-sovereignty projects;
Greenlandic autonomy / independence politics;
Danish, US, EU, Chinese, corporate, and UNP interests.

It is not a megacity. Its strategic importance comes from small nodes with global consequences.
Known Truth

Most settlements remain coastal and isolated from one another by road.
Movement depends on aircraft, ships, helicopters, drones, snow routes, local guides, and seasonal windows.
Agriculture has expanded only in limited southern and controlled greenhouse zones; Greenland is not a new global breadbasket.
Mineral, data, fishery, and logistics concessions are more important than open farmland.
Local consent and indigenous data/land sovereignty are constant fault lines.
Corporate development packages promise independence, jobs, cooling, clinics, ports, and connectivity while creating new dependency.

In-World Strategic Labels
Possible overlays:

Greenland Arctic Development Zone;
Kalaallit Climate Stabilization Concession;
Pituffik Meridian Security Area;
South Greenland Green Zone;
Disko Bay Fishery and Ice-Risk District;
Nuuk Receiver Finance Forum;
Northeast Sovereignty Patrol Area;
Kangerlussuaq Logistics Mandate.

Use bureaucratic labels before flashy cyberpunk labels.
Major Sites

Nuuk: capital, media/politics, development finance, UNP/corporate diplomacy.
Sisimiut: fishery, training, industry, mid-map logistics.
Ilulissat / Disko Bay: icefjord prestige, tourism, fisheries, climate symbolism.
Qaqortoq / Narsaq: southern green-zone agriculture, mining controversy, PR battle over “green land.”
Kangerlussuaq: air/logistics choke point.
Pituffik / Thule analogue: space, missile-warning, orbital traffic, polar White Sky telemetry.
Summit Station analogue: ice-sheet science, climate archives, extreme-environment operations.
Station Nord / Daneborg / Sirius patrol regions: sovereignty, wilderness, sensors, patrol myth.
Northeast Greenland National Park: remote research, wildlife, covert infrastructure.

Visual / Sensory Identity

Pale White Sky glare over black rock, ice, rust, snow, container yards, radar domes, fish plants, and hydro lines.
Neon signage as color against bleached daylight, not only night rain.
Warm interiors, harsh exteriors.
Helicopter pads, modular buildings, satellite dishes, fuel tanks, sled dogs, drones, snow machines, autonomous buoys.
Luxury blue-sky lounges beside cheap filter masks and broken public terminals.
Corporate green branding on extraction infrastructure.

Conflict Texture
Greenland is a battlezone without being a hot front:

lawfare;
development auctions;
election interference;
local council bribery;
cyber sabotage;
fishery quota manipulation;
mine protests;
data/provenance leaks;
convoy interdiction;
deniable Champion incidents;
private security “accidents.”

The tabloid/anarchist phrase for the situation can be bluntly vulgar: a corporate-state dick-measuring contest over who gets to “save” Greenland while owning it.
Related Pages

blue-week
white-sky
digital-net
world-map-and-political-economy
barents-research-group
qxz-meridian
greenland-blue-week-campaign

Open Questions

Should the public campaign title use Greenland, Kalaallit Nunaat, or a fictionalized region label?
Which settlement is the first player hub?
Which faction controls or claims the Greenland White Sky node?
How central should Greenlandic local politics be in the first campaign arc?
Is Blue Week a summit, a sky-break event, or deliberately both?

mysteries/blue-week.title: Blue Week
mysteries/blue-week.content:
Blue Week
One-Line Summary
Blue Week is both a campaign-era Arctic development spectacle and a real sky-break crisis: eco-anarchist sabotage, atmospheric counter-intervention, maintenance failure, or corporate false flag disrupts part of the white-sky, revealing real blue sky over greenland and triggering political panic, religious fervor, market crashes, and competing explanations.
Canon Status
Soft-canon draft. Blue Week should be a real event, not merely a fake feed incident. The new leading direction is that Greenland is the initial target / epicenter because it concentrates White Sky infrastructure, Arctic data, strategic routes, mineral concessions, UNP Net governance, corporate PR, and sovereignty politics.
What People Saw
For several days, the pale engineered ceiling thinned or opened in scattered Arctic regions. Some people saw blue sky without a screen, filter, or luxury simulation for the first time in their lives.
The event was uneven. Some towns saw only a blue tear near the horizon. Some ice routes saw hard blue daylight. Some corporate feeds showed nothing. Some Free-Net captures showed impossible colors. Some official models insisted the sky had remained within safe tolerance.
Public Face: The Summit
Before it became a crisis, Blue Week was already a name on calendars: Greenland’s development week, climate-adaptation expo, Arctic investment summit, UNP Net-security exercise, autonomy finance forum, and White Sky maintenance demonstration.
Delegations arrived to negotiate:

mineral concessions;
port and airfield upgrades;
fisheries and cold-chain systems;
satellite and sensor corridors;
Treaty Net / corporate grid gateways;
climate adaptation funding;
local consent packages;
White Sky maintenance liabilities.

Then the name became literal.
Competing Explanations

Eco-anarchist sabotage by Open Sky cells or related direct-action groups.
A White Sky maintenance failure at a Greenland / polar Meridian node.
Unauthorized regional tuning by Albedo Sovereignists.
Corporate false flag to justify emergency powers.
Corporate proof that the system could be relaxed safely.
Corporate proof that relaxing it would cause disaster.
UNP Net-security failure or AGI-quarantine incident.
Sensor/feed manipulation hiding a worse atmospheric event.
A religious sign, mass hallucination, or Digital-Net contamination of memory.

Several explanations may be partly true.
Greenland Importance
Greenland makes Blue Week stronger because it is not a generic stage. It is:

physically close to Arctic climate and satellite infrastructure;
politically contested through autonomy and outside development finance;
valuable for minerals, fisheries, routes, radar, weather, and data;
sparse enough to recover wilderness strategy;
public enough for Champions to matter as symbolic operators;
fragile enough that “just sabotage the node” has morally dangerous consequences.

Eco-Anarchist Reading
The strongest version of Blue Week is not anti-science primitivism. The eco-anarchists understand that the White Sky prevents mass death. Their claim is harsher: a livable planet has been converted into a corporate hostage system, and any survival that requires permanent proprietary maintenance is already a form of occupation.
Their opponents call them Terminationists because any large-scale failure could produce rapid heat rebound and mass casualties. The label is partly propaganda and partly fair warning.
Possible movement layers:

Atmospheric commons lawyers and climate-justice organizers.
Blue Restorationist mass politics, mostly nonviolent.
Open Sky cells willing to sabotage maintenance infrastructure.
Unceiling networks that publish leaked sky-model data.
Greenlandic anti-concession and autonomy groups, not all aligned with sabotage.
Religious or rural groups who interpret blue sky as return, mercy, or judgment.

The event should remain morally unstable: beautiful, politically clarifying, and potentially murderous.
Why It Matters
Blue Week makes the old sky emotionally and politically real. It can create:

the initial campaign crisis;
mass unrest against sky operators;
Sky Loyalist panic about termination risk;
Greenland development deals collapsing or accelerating;
new religious and ecological movements;
synthetic-reality provenance wars;
market crashes in climate-risk securities;
faction recruitment around the meaning of blue;
Champions whose public role begins during the event.

organizations/barents-research-group.title: Barents Research Group
organizations/barents-research-group.content:
Barents Research Group
One-Line Summary
Barents Research Group is an innocent-sounding polar research, maritime safety, and climate-risk corporation that became one of the world’s key Arctic megacorps by turning climate data, route certification, seabed mapping, extraction concessions, undersea cables, and polar security into one integrated control layer.
Canon Status
Reviewed soft-canon. The Arctic / polar exploitation megacorp direction is accepted. The name Barents Research Group / BRG is the current preferred name. Other proposed megacorps such as Hanseatic Resilience Group and Asterion Civic are not yet canonized.
What It Claims To Be
Barents Research Group presents itself as a scientific and humanitarian institution operating in the changing North.
Its public language is deliberately calm:

polar climate research;
fisheries monitoring;
permafrost and methane studies;
ice-route forecasting;
maritime safety;
search-and-rescue coordination;
environmental risk assessment;
Arctic infrastructure continuity;
White Sky polar calibration support.

It appears on treaty panels, shipping standards, insurer models, university partnerships, climate dashboards, and emergency-response exercises. Its reports are written like research papers. Its facilities look like observatories, logistics hubs, laboratories, and rescue stations rather than obvious fortresses.
What It Actually Controls
BRG’s power comes from the fact that Arctic exploitation depends on trusted data before it depends on visible force.
By the Neon Champions present, BRG controls or strongly influences:

Arctic shipping route certification;
autonomous icebreaker fleets;
seabed mapping and mineral surveys;
rare-earth and critical-mineral concessions;
offshore energy and port access;
undersea cable routes and repair priority;
polar satellite ground stations;
cold-climate data centers;
fisheries quota modeling;
permafrost methane accounting;
polar White Sky monitoring and calibration stations;
insurance risk scores for northern settlements, ports, mines, and routes;
private maritime security and rescue contracts.

If BRG says a route is safe, ships move. If BRG says a town, port, or mine is outside continuity parameters, insurance and credit vanish. If BRG certifies an extraction site as climate-critical, states tolerate damage they would otherwise condemn.
This makes BRG a plausible Great Corporate Person under the UNP order: not because it owns the Arctic outright, but because polar data, routes, minerals, cables, rescue, and climate archives have become continuity infrastructure.
Its unofficial internal doctrine is often summarized as:

What is measured can be claimed.

Origin
BRG likely began as a public-private Arctic monitoring consortium created when the poles became strategically unstable after the White Sky and the acceleration of northern resource competition.
Its early legitimacy came from work nobody else could coordinate cleanly:

measuring ice instability;
forecasting navigable polar windows;
mapping new seabed routes;
certifying rescue coverage;
reconciling insurer, state, shipping, climate, and military data;
protecting polar research stations and cables from sabotage;
maintaining sensor networks in politically sensitive waters.

The corporation became dangerous when it started buying the infrastructure its research had made valuable.
Corporate Mask
BRG’s name is intentionally non-threatening. It does not sound like an extraction combine, private navy, or Arctic cartel. It sounds like a research body.
That mask matters. BRG’s authority rests on neutrality, scientific competence, and the impression that it is merely describing reality. In practice, its descriptions make reality: viable route, unsafe route, protected settlement, abandoned settlement, climate-critical mine, illegal fishery, rescue-priority corridor, insured infrastructure, stranded population.
Major Divisions
Barents Cryodata
Polar data centers, climate archives, White Sky telemetry, ice models, permafrost records, and long-term environmental custody.
Heroic face: preserves climate data in hardened northern facilities.
Horrific face: controls which models, baselines, and archives are treated as legally real.
Barents Marine Survey
Seabed mapping, mineral scans, undersea cable routes, autonomous survey craft, offshore hazard certification, and disputed continental-shelf evidence.
Heroic face: reduces shipping and extraction accidents.
Horrific face: maps resources before local populations, indigenous authorities, or weaker states can contest the claim.
Barents Route Safety
Shipping certification, autonomous icebreaker scheduling, rescue contracts, port continuity, route insurance, and emergency maritime corridors.
Heroic face: keeps northern trade from becoming a death lottery.
Horrific face: turns navigation into a subscription regime. Uncertified ships, settlements, and ports effectively disappear from the insured world.
Barents Materials
Critical minerals, rare earths, nickel, cobalt, platinum-group metals, battery inputs, cold-region extraction concessions, and recycling claims.
Heroic face: supplies the materials needed for grids, prosthetics, drones, batteries, climate systems, and reconstruction.
Horrific face: treats polar landscapes as a necessary sacrifice zone for the maintained world.
Barents Security & Rescue
Nominally a polar rescue and emergency-response arm. Functionally a private Arctic navy and security service protecting cables, ports, mines, icebreakers, research stations, and sanctioned routes.
Heroic face: saves crews and settlements in impossible conditions.
Horrific face: decides who is rescued, who is trespassing, and who is an infrastructure threat.
Geographic Reach
BRG’s center of gravity is the Barents / European Arctic, but its influence extends across the whole Arctic-subarctic frontier:

Barents Sea;
Svalbard routes and research zones;
northern Norway and Finland;
Greenland-linked mineral and cable corridors;
Arctic Russia gray-market concessions;
North Atlantic cable and shipping approaches;
polar satellite and sensor infrastructure.

It may have rivals or sister structures around the Bering Strait and North Pacific, but those are not yet canonized.
Relationship to Other Setting Forces
White Sky
The White Sky makes BRG indispensable. Polar albedo, ice behavior, cloud interactions, atmospheric monitoring, and northern-route volatility all require dense sensor networks and disputed climate models.
BRG does not need to have created the White Sky. QXZ Meridian is the leading candidate for the first mover; BRG profits from being one of the institutions that measures, certifies, and maintains the polar parts of the world the White Sky made newly valuable.
Vezha Systems
BRG likely buys drones, counter-drone systems, autonomous-security stacks, and hardened logistics software from Vezha Systems. Their relationship is practical rather than friendly: Vezha knows war; BRG knows ice, insurance, extraction, and route legality.
The two companies overlap in contested territories where Arctic routes, damaged Russian assets, Baltic security, and postwar concessions meet.
Kantograd
Kantograd is a natural brokerage zone for BRG: Russian Arctic assets, sanction-bent components, Baltic shipping, insurance workarounds, and disputed scientific data can all pass through its treaty/freeport ambiguity.
Digital-Net
BRG’s polar data networks, cable routes, sensor basins, and cold data centers make it deeply entangled with the Digital-Net. The farther north one goes, the more reality depends on trusted feeds: weather, ice, rescue windows, cable status, mining boundaries, fishery quotas, drone corridors, and atmospheric calibration.
Public Face
Possible slogans:

Research for a Changing North.


Continuity Through Understanding.


Mapping the Future of the Poles.

The company prefers images of research vessels, ice stations, clean dashboards, quiet satellite domes, rescued crews, protected fisheries, and serious scientists in white glare.
Horrific Version
BRG is not evil because it hates nature. It is frightening because it is rational, necessary, and legally trusted.
Its darkest acts can look like maintenance decisions:

declaring a settlement outside rescue continuity;
certifying an extraction concession as climate-critical;
downgrading an indigenous claim because its data is deemed insufficient;
reclassifying a fishing ground after a proprietary model update;
routing cables through contested seabeds before local politics catch up;
treating protest vessels as route-safety threats;
delaying rescue to protect insured assets first;
making Arctic exploitation feel like sober planetary management.

Heroic Version
The heroic version is also real. BRG’s systems prevent shipwrecks, famine, cable collapse, mining disasters, and climate-data loss. Some polar communities may depend on BRG rescue, telemetry, medicine, and logistics to survive.
This makes resistance complicated: attacking BRG may also attack the infrastructure keeping people alive.
Game / Story Uses

Arctic campaign-map power controlling route access, minerals, weather data, and rescue priority.
Employer for polar missions that begin as science/rescue and become extraction/security operations.
Antagonist in indigenous sovereignty, climate-data, or sacrificed-settlement stories.
Source of rare resources for drones, body mods, batteries, White Sky maintenance, and compute infrastructure.
Custodian of climate archives whose records could prove or disprove White Sky harm.
Owner of cold data centers where Echoes, models, and forbidden archives may be stored.

Open Questions

Is BRG still formally headquartered in a Nordic jurisdiction, or has it become a treaty-layered holding structure?
Does BRG operate under public scientific charters, private concession law, or Arctic emergency authority?
Are there Bering / Pacific-Arctic rivals, or is BRG already global across the whole polar frontier?
Which indigenous, local, state, or activist groups most visibly oppose BRG?
Does BRG control any White Sky calibration infrastructure directly, or only the polar data that others depend on?
Which Champion, if any, is associated with Arctic resistance, rescue, extraction, or BRG security?

organizations/chorus-exchange.title: Chorus Exchange
organizations/chorus-exchange.content:
Chorus Exchange
One-Line Summary
Chorus Exchange is the ninth Great Corporate Person: a media, communications, creator-economy, payment, remittance, advertising, subscription, and reputation-market megacorp that controls attention and liquidity continuity.
Canon Status
Reviewed soft-canon. The roster has expanded from eight to nine Great Corporate Persons so Chorus can exist alongside Janus-Kestrel Continuity Group rather than being folded into it.
This preserves an important boundary:

Janus-Kestrel carries, clears, routes, and relays through hard infrastructure.
Chorus amplifies, monetizes, settles, ranks, and socially distributes.

Continuity Layer
Chorus controls attention and liquidity continuity.
It does not decide whether a fact is legally true. That is Axiom.
It does not own lawful cognition or frontier model custody. That is Helvetia.
It does not operate the port gate, customs seal, cable landing, or orbital relay. That is Janus-Kestrel.
Chorus owns the layer where people:

speak;
stream;
organize;
follow;
subscribe;
pay;
tip;
borrow;
advertise;
receive wages;
sell work;
join publics;
become visible;
become fundable;
become socially reachable.

Public Claim

Everyone has a voice and a way to be paid.

Chorus sells itself as the world’s civic interface: payment rails for the unbanked, reach for creators, emergency cash transfers, safe subscriptions, small-merchant settlement, reputation portability, multilingual messaging, cultural distribution, and anti-disinformation partnerships.
Some of this is true.
Dark Claim

If Chorus cannot monetize you, you become socially silent and financially thin.

Chorus does not need to erase people. It can make them hard to find, hard to fund, hard to pay, hard to recommend, hard to insure, hard to invite, hard to sponsor, hard to convert into a public.
Why It Deserves the Ninth Seat
By 2052, Chorus freezing or defecting would not merely break entertainment.
It would disrupt:

creator income;
small merchant payments;
remittances;
payroll rails;
subscription credentials;
school and work messaging;
emergency cash transfers;
municipal public alerts;
political campaign outreach;
reputation-based market access;
mutual-aid coordination;
ad-funded public media;
Champion fan economies;
sponsorship pipelines;
donation and bounty markets;
local informal commerce.

That is civilizationally load-bearing enough for Great Person status.
Formation Logic
Phase 1 — Platform Convergence
Chorus begins as a post-2030s convergence of social platforms, short-video networks, creator payment systems, super-app messaging, ad exchanges, remittance rails, consumer credit, payroll fintech, streaming services, influencer agencies, and subscription bundles.
No single legacy company survives unchanged. Chorus is a treaty-recognized holding structure built from assets that were too politically important, too financially entangled, and too socially embedded to simply nationalize.
Phase 2 — Synthetic Feed Collapse
The spread of synthetic media, fraud, VI-generated persuasion, identity spoofing, deepfake celebrities, automated cults, and mass-scale social manipulation produces a public legitimacy crisis.
Axiom handles admissibility and provenance.
Chorus handles circulation, monetization, ranking, reach, and settlement.
The two are not the same. That distinction is one reason both become powerful.
Phase 3 — Liquidity Capture
Payments, media, and social reach fuse because attention alone is no longer enough. Every voice needs payment routing, subscription handling, identity risk scoring, tax logic, donation controls, advertiser safety, reputation transfer, and automated compliance.
Chorus becomes the place where social existence and microfinance meet.
Phase 4 — Champion Economy
Champions make Chorus politically unavoidable.
A Champion is not only a fighter or altered body. A Champion is often a public. Their value exists partly in the crowd around them: fans, enemies, sponsors, faction channels, faction myths, scandal markets, combat feeds, tribute economies, copycat body-mod trends, cults, betting pools, donation drives, and recruitment funnels.
Chorus becomes the main industrial system for turning Champion presence into money, morale, legitimacy, and movement.
Champion Relationship
Chorus is one of the main reasons Championhood can become a strategic category rather than just an elite-soldier label.
It can:

create a Champion’s public;
rank Champions across incompatible factions;
syndicate combat feeds;
sell sponsorship bundles;
amplify martyrdom stories;
bury scandals;
fund rebel icons through microdonations;
demonetize anti-corporate Champions;
route bounty markets;
sell biometric fan experiences;
package Echo interviews;
manufacture “rivalries” between Champions;
turn battlefield footage into recruitment;
convert parasocial devotion into faction capital.

Chorus does not have to own a Champion’s body to own much of their aura.
Champion Instruments
Chorus Rings — official ranking bands for player-facing Champion tiers, nominally based on reach, field relevance, sponsor risk, verified deeds, and public resonance. Critics call them “stock tickers for demigods.”
Patron Channels — subscription-publics around Champions. Some are ordinary fan clubs; some are cults, intelligence operations, mercenary recruiting pools, or money-laundering fronts.
Saint Clips — short, hyper-edited miracle moments: rescues, duels, survivals, betrayals, last words. Often more politically important than the full event.
Resonance Scores — proprietary metrics estimating whether a Champion can move people: recruitment, donations, fear, morale, riots, imitation, purchase behavior, surrender likelihood.
Chorus Bounties — public or semi-public financial incentives attached to sightings, rescues, defeats, interviews, defections, scandals, or relic recovery.
Echo Features — interviews and simulations involving dead or missing Champions, legally constrained by Axiom but packaged by Chorus.
Corporate Structure
Chorus Network
Messaging, feeds, channels, streams, civic alerts, public rooms, creator profiles, reputation surfaces.
Public face: voice and connection.
Dark face: reach throttling, attention rationing, recommendation warfare.
Chorus Pay
Payments, remittances, creator payouts, small merchant settlement, payroll routing, emergency cash transfers.
Public face: economic inclusion.
Dark face: liquidity discipline and soft debanking.
Chorus Market
Advertising exchange, sponsorship marketplace, creator-brand deals, influencer procurement, political ad controls, faction-safe messaging.
Public face: creators can live from their work.
Dark face: publics become purchasable inventory.
ChoirRank
Reputation, discovery, trend arbitration, Champion rankings, creator safety tiers, public resonance scoring.
Public face: quality and safety.
Dark face: social visibility as corporate policy.
Patron House
Subscription bundles, fan clubs, Champion patron channels, faction communities, cult-risk moderation, exclusive streams.
Public face: community support.
Dark face: parasocial monetization at industrial scale.
CivicPulse
Municipal alerting, disaster communications, election reminders, public-health messaging, ration notices, evacuation messages.
Public face: public service.
Dark face: a city that loses CivicPulse loses the habit of collective action.
Chorus Credit
Microcredit, creator advances, reputation-backed loans, wage smoothing, disaster liquidity, subscription collateral.
Public face: access to working capital.
Dark face: attention-backed debt.
Anthem Safety
Content moderation, advertiser safety, political-risk compliance, VI persuasion audits, narrative threat response.
Public face: safer public spaces.
Dark face: privatized propaganda triage.
Backstage Bureau
Talent management, Champion media training, scandal containment, defection negotiation, image insurance, grief releases after death.
Public face: professional support.
Dark face: myth maintenance.
Geography
Chorus is deliberately multi-seated.
Los Angeles / Mexico City — entertainment, streaming, celebrity machinery, Latin American creator economies.
Singapore / Jakarta — super-app governance, cross-border payments, Southeast Asian social commerce.
Lagos / Nairobi — mobile money, creator publics, remittance corridors, informal-market finance.
São Paulo / Buenos Aires — social-commerce finance, political media, fandom economies.
Mumbai / Bengaluru — mass messaging, payment rails, creator scale, moderation labor, language systems.
Seoul / Tokyo — idol culture, synthetic celebrity, fan monetization, reputation engineering.
Dubai / Abu Dhabi — capital, influencer finance, image insurance, exile media.
Brussels / Dublin / Luxembourg — regulatory interfaces, platform law, tax routing, advertiser standards.
Tallinn / Helsinki — identity/provenance integrations with Axiom-adjacent systems, civic messaging resilience, postwar registry/feed recovery.
Relationships With Other Great Persons
Axiom
Axiom authenticates persons, records, evidence, feed provenance, and legal reality. Chorus distributes and monetizes visibility.
Cooperation: verified public channels, anti-fraud payments, election messaging, Echo rights, birth/death/scandal records.
Conflict: Axiom may say something is authentic; Chorus may still suppress it as unsafe, unmonetizable, or destabilizing. Chorus may make a false story socially dominant before Axiom can make the true one legally admissible.
Boundary line:

Axiom says whether it is real. Chorus decides whether anyone sees it, funds it, or cares.

Helvetia
Helvetia governs lawful cognition and model custody. Chorus depends on constrained VI for ranking, moderation, translation, ad placement, persuasion auditing, fraud detection, and creator tools.
Conflict: Chorus constantly wants more predictive autonomy than the AGI Compact comfortably permits. It does not need forbidden AGI to be dangerous; population-scale non-AGI persuasion systems are enough.
Janus-Kestrel Continuity Group
Janus-Kestrel carries hard signals and physical movement. Chorus rides those channels and turns reach into money and publics.
Conflict: Janus-Kestrel can degrade a region’s relay or corridor priority; Chorus can make that degradation politically invisible or explosive.
QXZ Meridian
QXZ Meridian needs public legitimacy for White Sky and adaptation finance. Chorus sells climate messaging, adaptation subscriptions, public-risk campaigns, and denial management.
Conflict: Chorus can amplify monsoon-theft movements, climate martyr Champions, or QXZ-approved “rational adaptation” propaganda depending on incentives.
Vezha Systems
Vezha Systems produces combat feeds, battlefield legends, civil-defense heroics, and martyr economies that Chorus packages.
Conflict: Vezha wants operational secrecy; Chorus wants morale, recruitment, donations, and spectacle.
Verdant
Verdant uses Chorus for Feed the World messaging, donor dashboards, famine alerts, ration-app communications, and reputational defense.
Conflict: Chorus can make hunger visible, invisible, sentimental, or blameable.
Vitae Continuity
Vitae provides bodies; Chorus provides body aspiration and anxiety.
Conflict: copycat Champion modifications and sponsorship trends can drive dangerous prosthetic, fertility, or biotech demand that Vitae then monetizes.
Street-Level Consequences

A musician, street preacher, Champion, or rebel cell may be “alive” politically only while Chorus keeps routing attention and money.
A neighborhood can be materially poor but politically dangerous if Chorus resonance spikes there.
Soft debanking is more common than formal censorship: payments fail, sponsors flee, subscriptions freeze, ads demonetize.
“Going quiet” means losing reach, payment routing, chat access, subscriber visibility, and reputation portability at once.
A dead Champion may earn more after martyrdom than in life.
False Champions can become real political forces if Chorus publics stabilize around them.
Fan economies can finance militias, clinics, lawsuits, refugee corridors, body modifications, and assassinations.
A popular Champion can move markets without issuing orders.

Common Slang

Choired — amplified by Chorus, often suspiciously.
Muted — suppressed without formal ban.
Greylisted — payment and reach degraded but not cut off.
Thin money — funds that technically exist but fail in high-risk contexts.
Saint clip — viral heroic/martyrdom fragment.
Patron swarm — fan-funded mobilization around a Champion or cause.
Dead channel — a public whose reach and payments were silently severed.
Choirboy / Choirgirl — paid narrative operator; can be affectionate or insulting.

Game / Story Uses

A faction hires the player to protect a Champion’s Patron Channel during a scandal.
A rebel Champion is not defeated in combat but greylisted into irrelevance.
A dead Champion’s Echo Feature starts riots after Chorus releases an edited interview.
A city loses CivicPulse during a heatwave and panic spreads faster than official alerts.
Chorus bounties turn civilians into informants.
A player must choose between exposing a true atrocity and giving Chorus the martyr footage it wants.
A fake Champion created by edits, bots, and carefully routed payments becomes symbolically real.
A campaign map objective is not a mine or fortress but a Chorus resonance hub.

Open Questions

Does Chorus directly sponsor Champions, or mostly monetize every faction’s Champions?
Does it operate official Champion rankings, or only “unofficial” rankings everyone uses?
Are some player heroes ex-Chorus assets, cancelled stars, manufactured rivals, or deliberately unmonetizable anti-Champions?
How closely does Chorus cooperate with Axiom in verifying Champion footage?
Which faction most hates Chorus: anti-corporate rebels, religious anti-idol groups, state broadcasters, or old banks?

organizations/great-corporate-persons.title: Great Corporate Persons
organizations/great-corporate-persons.content:
Great Corporate Persons
One-Line Summary
The Great Corporate Persons are the tiny class of megacorps recognized inside the UNP because each controls a continuity layer the world cannot safely abandon, nationalize, or destroy without risking systemic collapse.
Canon Status
Reviewed soft-canon. The formula is accepted for now: roughly nine Great Corporate Persons are recognized because each controls a continuity layer that can sustain or endanger civilization. The roster expanded from eight to nine when Chorus Exchange became necessary as a distinct attention/liquidity layer rather than being folded into Janus-Kestrel.
What They Are
A Great Corporate Person is not merely a large company. It is a corporation, trust-network, treaty vehicle, or holding structure whose infrastructure has become civilizationally load-bearing.
Recognition is not a prize. It is a bargain.
A recognized corporate person receives:

formal standing in UNP processes;
access to crisis councils;
protection for declared continuity infrastructure;
sanctions coordination against attacks on its protected systems;
arbitration channels;
legitimacy in procurement and insurance markets.

In exchange, it accepts:

AGI/ASI compact obligations;
compute and model inspections where relevant;
continuity duties;
emergency operating plans;
disclosure rituals;
sanctions compliance;
liability arbitration;
charter review of systemically dangerous conduct.

In practice, the exchange favors incumbents. But it also gives the world some leverage over them.
Why There Are So Few
Many corporations are rich. Few are existentially entangled with survival.
A Great Corporate Person must control at least one continuity layer:

atmosphere and climate maintenance;
frontier compute and model custody;
war and civil-defense operating systems;
food, seed, nutrient, or famine logistics;
body, organ, prosthetic, fertility, or adaptation infrastructure;
identity, feed provenance, civil registry, or Echo legality;
ports, cables, orbital relays, customs, or global logistics;
attention, media reach, payments, remittances, subscriptions, and liquidity access;
polar routes, critical minerals, rescue, and climate archives.

The number nine is the current target. It remains small enough for myth and politics, but large enough to give media/finance its own continuity layer rather than collapsing it into logistics or identity.
Recognized / Strong Candidates
QXZ Meridian
QXZ Meridian is the strongest current Great Person candidate. It controls the continuity stack around White Sky maintenance, adaptation biotech, climate-risk insurance, agrigen, liability science, and Meridian Stations.
Continuity layer: atmosphere / adaptation / climate-risk arbitration.
Public claim: it keeps the climate survivable.
Dark claim: it made survival proprietary.
Vezha Systems
Vezha Systems is the accepted Ukrainian-origin war-OS, drone, civil-defense, and resilience megacorp.
Continuity layer: survival under attack / battlefield and city-resilience coordination.
Public claim: it lets smaller powers and cities survive aggression.
Dark claim: it makes permanent limited war administratively efficient.
Barents Research Group
Barents Research Group is the accepted polar research, route-certification, extraction, cable, rescue, and Arctic data megacorp.
Continuity layer: polar routes / critical minerals / northern data and rescue.
Public claim: it makes a changing Arctic navigable and safe.
Dark claim: it turns measurement into ownership.
Helvetia
Helvetia is the accepted frontier compute, model custody, chip attestation, sovereign cloud, and AGI Compact safeguards megacorp.
Continuity layer: lawful cognition / frontier compute custody / model nonproliferation.
Public claim: it prevents threshold catastrophe.
Dark claim: it froze lawful cognition inside incumbent custody.
Strong Candidates Under Review
Axiom
Axiom is the current recommended candidate for the identity, feed-provenance, civil registry, evidence, and Echo-recognition slot. It is the public name of the post-merger Axiom-SOVRAN trust stack; Axiom Tallinn survives as a regional registry-recovery unit, not the parent megacorp brand.
Continuity layer: civil reality / identity / provenance / admissibility.
Public claim: it protects identity, records, evidence, elections, property, humanitarian aid, and media authenticity from synthetic collapse.
Dark claim: it makes truth and personhood administratively revocable.
Verdant
Verdant is the current recommended candidate for the food, nutrient, seed, crop-risk, grain-routing, emergency-ration, fermentation-protein, and nutrient-recovery slot. Its formal style is probably Verdant Covenant Group, but ordinary usage is just Verdant.
Continuity layer: food / nutrient / seed / famine logistics.
Public claim: it prevents famine through resilient seed systems, nutrient circularity, crop-risk intelligence, grain logistics, and emergency food provisioning.
Dark claim: it turned hunger into an administrable market condition.
Additional Strong Candidates / Recent Seats
Some of these are not yet full organization pages; others have now been promoted into the nine-seat roster.
Body and Health Continuity
Recommended leading candidate: Vitae Continuity, documented in megacorp-7-body-continuity-2026-05-22.
Continuity layer: body continuity / organ systems / prosthetics / fertility / workforce viability / biological uptime.
Public claim: No life interrupted.
Dark claim: you do not own your body’s remaining value.
Boundary: QXZ Meridian owns survival conditions and climate exposure; Vitae owns biological uptime after those conditions reach the body.
Food / Nutrient / Seed Logistics
This slot is now represented by the Verdant reviewed soft-canon candidate.
Core risk remains: avoid making it just “Monsanto but bigger.” Its real power should be famine avoidance, calorie insurance, nutrient circularity, ration thresholds, and the failed-harvest protocol.
Identity / Feed Provenance
This slot is now represented by the Axiom reviewed soft-canon candidate.
Core risk remains: do not make it generic social media. Make it the institution that decides what counts as legally real, admissible, recoverable, and recordable.
Ports / Cables / Orbital Logistics
Recommended leading candidate: Janus-Kestrel Continuity Group, documented in megacorp-8-threshold-logistics-2026-05-22 and revised in janus-kestrel-media-finance-nadir-2026-05-22.
Continuity layer: lawful movement / thresholds / customs / port, cable, drone, and orbital interfaces / cargo and signal legitimacy.
Public claim: Continuity is civilization.
Dark claim: nothing moves, arrives, clears, or relays unless Janus-Kestrel recognizes it.
Boundary: Barents Research Group certifies polar frontiers; Janus-Kestrel decides whether goods, people, bandwidth, repairs, and exceptions can circulate through the global system.
Chorus Exchange
Chorus Exchange is the ninth Great Corporate Person: the media, communications, creator-economy, payment, remittance, advertising, subscription, and reputation-market megacorp.
Continuity layer: attention and liquidity continuity.
Public claim: everyone has a voice and a way to be paid.
Dark claim: if Chorus cannot monetize you, you become socially silent and financially thin.
Champion relevance: Chorus is closely tied to Champions because it manufactures, ranks, amplifies, monetizes, and sometimes destroys the publics around them. It can make a Champion into a saint, brand, scandal, martyr, market signal, recruitment funnel, or politically toxic silence.
Boundary: Axiom says whether something is real; Chorus decides whether anyone sees it, funds it, or cares. Helvetia governs lawful cognition; Chorus uses constrained VI persuasion and ranking systems below the forbidden AGI threshold. Janus-Kestrel carries signals and goods; Chorus monetizes and amplifies the publics carried across those channels.
Political Logic
The Great Persons are recognized because they can credibly threaten the order even without making threats.
If QXZ fails, climate maintenance may collapse.
If Vezha withdraws, cities and borders may become undefended.
If BRG withholds data, Arctic routes, cables, and mineral claims become legally unstable.
If Helvetia defects, the AGI compact may fail.
If an identity/provenance company lies, elections, casualties, land claims, and Echo personhood can become unknowable.
If Verdant withholds continuity status, food can exist in warehouses while hunger remains administratively unrecognized.
If Vitae withdraws body continuity, people can remain alive but functionally nonviable.
If Janus-Kestrel denies clearance or relay priority, medicine, food, organs, refugees, repair crews, and emergency signals can exist at the gate but fail to arrive.
If Chorus withdraws reach or liquidity, a person, movement, Champion, neighborhood, or small economy can remain legally real while becoming socially silent and financially thin.
This is why states hate them, need them, regulate them, subsidize them, and invite them into the room.
Internal Contradiction
The Great Persons are charter-bound because they are too important to leave unregulated.
They are powerful because charter recognition tells the world they are too important to attack.
The same rule that disciplines them also entrenches them.
Public Face
They prefer to say they are not sovereign.
They say they are:

continuity providers;
chartered persons;
infrastructure custodians;
emergency partners;
accountable operators;
responsible innovators;
treaty-bound service entities.

Their critics say these are just softer words for private sovereignty.
Game / Story Uses

Natural top-level sponsors for factions without making every faction a corporation.
Strategic equivalents of great houses, but grounded in infrastructure rather than bloodlines.
Campaign-map powers that can shape conflict through service access, not only armies.
Sources of Champions as corporate saints, deniable assets, defectors, inspectors, or treaty anomalies.
A roster-building frame for the nine largest megacorps.

Open Questions

Is the number exactly nine in the charter, or just the present count after Chorus Exchange was added?
Are Great Person recognitions permanent, renewable, inheritable, or revocable?
Can a state-owned enterprise become a Great Person?
Can a city compact, labor federation, university trust, indigenous authority, or Echo estate become a non-corporate Person?
Is Verdant Covenant Group the right formal style, or should “Covenant” remain treaty language while the legal parent is even drier?
Should the body-continuity slot become Vitae Continuity, or does Continuance Health Combine / SomaDyne fit better?
Should the threshold-logistics slot become Janus-Kestrel Continuity Group? Current direction: yes, because Janus gives thresholds while Kestrel gives speed, drones, couriers, relays, and aerial/orbital movement.
How openly does Chorus Exchange sponsor Champions versus merely monetizing and ranking every faction’s Champions?
Do any Great Persons secretly sponsor accelerationist AGI work while publicly enforcing the compact?
