pain access;
fertility storage;
treatment priority;
organ eligibility;
replacement schedules;
occupational clearance.

Street slang:

greenbody — fully covered and continuity-certified.
greybody — partially covered, downgraded, debt-burdened, or medically uncertain.
deadwalking — alive but no longer eligible for meaningful continuity support.
body lien — debt attached to organ, prosthetic, fertility, or treatment access.
socket debt — prosthetic maintenance debt.

Relationships With Existing Great Persons
QXZ Meridian
Strategic partner and actuarial rival.
QXZ Meridian declares climate exposure and adaptation risk. Vitae manages the body after exposure becomes damage.
Conflict: QXZ wants preventive adaptation; Vitae profits from continuous repair. QXZ wants fewer heat strokes; Vitae sells renal support, prosthetic cooling, and heat-injury recovery.
Possible treaty: a Meridian-Vitae Partition Accord separating exposure risk from continuity risk.
Tryzub Systems
Military rehabilitation partner and prosthetic-control rival.
Tryzub Systems needs soldiers, veterans, drone crews, and civilians repaired. Vitae owns much of the hardware and recovery chain.
Conflict: Tryzub wants tactical prosthetics under battlefield command architecture. Vitae wants clinical safety, subscription maintenance, and warranty control.
Street hook: veterans with split-stack bodies — Tryzub tactical firmware over Vitae medical hardware.
Barents Research Group
Frontier labor body partner.
Barents Research Group uses bodies in cold, isolated, extractive frontiers. Vitae repairs frostbite, lung damage, bone stress, trauma, and reproductive strain.
Conflict: Barents treats workers as mission assets; Vitae treats them as continuity contracts.
Helvetia
Legal-compute and medical-arbitration partner.
Helvetia certifies lawful models for treatment authorization, consent, liability, and cross-border medical arbitration.
Conflict: Helvetia may certify a procedure as lawful while Vitae uses delay as economic triage. Appeals may be legal and still slower than organ failure.
Axiom
Personhood and body-record dependency.
Axiom certifies identity, consent trails, births, deaths, organ provenance, embryo ownership, and civil continuity. Vitae wants biological continuity to influence civil status.
Core dispute: if most of your body is replaced, your embryos are in lien, your prosthetic eyes are licensed, and your immune system is externally maintained, who certifies that you are still you?
Verdant
Famine medicine and reproductive-triage partner.
Verdant feeds populations. Vitae decides which bodies receive prenatal support, pediatric care, renal recovery, artificial gestation, or malnutrition repair.
Conflict: Verdant’s Feed the World clinics may become Vitae recruitment funnels for desperate families.
Street-Level Consequences

A dockworker’s arm works at full torque only while their employer plan is paid.
A veteran’s limbs lock during a protest because Tryzub and Vitae disagree over control status.
A family can keep stored embryos only if fertility debt remains serviced.
A patient is alive but classified as deadwalking after continuity downgrade.
Underground body shops jailbreak limbs, spoof immune compliance, and clone maintenance keys.
Poor districts have visible modular bodies; elite districts have seamless synthetic skin.
Transit gates reject people whose body records mismatch Axiom identity.
A child saved by SecondSun is enrolled into biometric debt for life.

Game / Story Hooks

Steal prosthetic firmware keys from SomaDyne.
Protect an illegal organ courier from RedCell and Axiom inspectors.
Expose KinForge embryo lien fraud.
Rescue a worker marked nonviable by Atlas Occupational Viability.
Break into a continuity tribunal before an organ appeal expires.
Help Axiom prove someone is legally continuous after reconstruction.
Defend a street clinic from Vitae contract enforcement.
Investigate a Verdant/Vitae famine pregnancy program.
Smuggle a veteran’s body stack out of Tryzub/Vitae jurisdiction.
Decide whether to leak a cure that would destroy a profitable chronic-care subscription line.

Recommendation
Develop Vitae Continuity next if the user accepts the slot.
Use SomaDyne Prosthetics, KinForge Reproductive, Continuum Organics, and Atlas Occupational Viability as the major immediately legible subsidiaries.
Do not make Vitae a generic hospital/pharma company. Its power is that it owns the continuity layer between being alive and being functionally viable.

raw/brainstorms/megacorp-8-threshold-log.title: Megacorp 8 — Threshold Logistics Brainstorm
raw/brainstorms/megacorp-8-threshold-log.content:
Megacorp 8 — Threshold Logistics Brainstorm
Short Recommendation
The eighth Great Corporate Person should probably be the threshold logistics megacorp: ports, customs, cable landings, orbital relays, bonded corridors, emergency routing, cargo identity, and lawful movement.
Leading candidate:

Janus-Kestrel Continuity Group

Short form:

Janus-Kestrel / Janus

Continuity layer:

lawful movement / thresholds / customs / port, cable, drone, and orbital interfaces / cargo and signal legitimacy

Public claim:

Continuity is civilization.

Dark claim:

Nothing moves unless Janus says it is real.

Core line:

Janus-Kestrel owns the world’s thresholds: the port gate, the customs seal, the cable landing, the drone corridor, the orbital relay, and the emergency exception.

This should not be a generic shipping company. A pure shipping megacorp is too narrow and too old-fashioned. The 2052 power is not owning every vessel. It is owning the interfaces that decide whether cargo, people, bandwidth, repair crews, medicine, grain, organs, drones, satellites, or refugees may cross from one legal/physical state into another.
Janus-Kestrel Revision
The stronger current naming direction is Janus-Kestrel Continuity Group rather than plain Janus.

Janus preserves gates, customs, law, thresholds, and exceptions.
Kestrel adds speed, aerial routes, drone corridors, courier networks, relay operations, and predatory precision.

The fused name lets the corporation contain two cultures: Janus offices of law, customs, treaty clearance, and bonded ledgers; Kestrel operations of drones, relays, couriers, emergency airbridges, and orbital handoffs.
This revision is expanded in janus-kestrel-media-finance-nadir-2026-05-22.
Why This Slot Belongs in the Final Eight
The current roster covers climate, war, polar frontiers, compute, identity, food, and likely bodies. What remains missing is circulation.
Movement is a strategic layer for the game:

supply lines;
map access;
smuggling;
sanctions evasion;
orbital logistics;
port sabotage;
cable repair;
customs blacklists;
humanitarian corridors;
drone and autonomous convoy routes;
who can move through a gate, checkpoint, port, bonded zone, or launch window.

Cyberpunk settings need a corporation that controls arteries and gates, not only minds and products. Janus adds visible spaces: ports, container yards, cable landings, orbital relay fields, bonded cities, customs courts, warehouse zones, drone corridors, launch pads, repair ships, and “temporary” disaster gates that become permanent concessions.
Pushback and Boundary With Barents
The risk is overlap with Barents Research Group. Barents already touches Arctic routes, polar cables, minerals, route certification, rescue, and frontier infrastructure.
Do not let Janus become “Barents but global.”
The clean split:
Barents Research Group is the polar frontier certifier and extractive/route science authority.
It asks:

Is this polar route physically possible?
Is this ice shelf, seabed, mineral zone, or high-latitude cable corridor certifiable?
What is the Arctic risk model?
Which polar port, icebreaker, mine, or cable path meets technical standard?

Janus Continuity Group is the global interface operator and customs-continuity authority.
It asks:

Can cargo from that route enter the world system?
Which customs identity does it carry?
Which port receives it?
Which relay authenticates it?
Which bonded corridor moves it inland?
Which emergency priority does it have?
Which exceptions apply?

Boundary phrase:

Barents certifies the frontier. Janus decides whether anything from it can circulate.

This preserves both.
Real-World Roots
Port Operators and Free Zones
Real roots: DP World, PSA International, Hutchison Ports, APM Terminals, Eurogate, ICTSI, China Merchants-style port concessions, Jebel Ali, Singapore, Rotterdam, Tangier Med, Panama, bonded free zones.
2052 extrapolation: automated terminals, private port cybersecurity, extraterritorial customs yards, bonded warehouse cities, labor credential systems, drone tug corridors, and continuity zones.
Shipping and Freight Platforms
Real roots: Maersk, MSC, CMA CGM, Hapag-Lloyd, DHL, Kuehne+Nagel, FedEx, Flexport, TradeLens-style digital freight experiments, container visibility systems.
2052 extrapolation: Janus does not need to own all ships. It owns berth access, port operating software, customs identity, route priority, insurance triggers, and emergency exception status.
Customs, Certification, and Inspection
Real roots: SGS, Bureau Veritas, Intertek, DNV, GS1, customs single windows, WCO-adjacent modernization, sanctions compliance vendors, export-control classification, KYC/AML for trade.
2052 extrapolation: customs becomes too complex for states alone. Janus runs tariff classification models, beneficial-ownership maps, sanctions logic, hazardous-cargo rules, dual-use scoring, and trusted cargo ledgers.
Cable Landings and Data Exchanges
Real roots: Equinix, Digital Realty, submarine cable landing stations, SubCom, NEC, Alcatel Submarine Networks, Orange Marine, cable repair consortia, internet exchange points.
2052 extrapolation: cable landing is not just telecom. It is customs for data and operational continuity for ports, hospitals, orbital relays, insurers, and military deconfliction.
Orbital Relays and Launch Interfaces
Real roots: Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper, SES, Intelsat, Iridium, ground stations, launch windows, smallsat logistics, maritime satellite networks.
2052 extrapolation: orbital communications, emergency store-and-forward, surface/orbit cargo slots, relay partitions, and launch customs become part of movement authority.
Chokepoint Crisis Finance
Real roots: Lloyd’s markets, marine insurance, war-risk premiums, Suez/Panama chokepoints, Red Sea disruptions, Black Sea grain corridor, sanctions, catastrophe bonds.
2052 extrapolation: route availability becomes a financial product. Janus sells continuity options, berth futures, cable repair priority, corridor guarantees, and humanitarian exception bonds.
Formation Logic
Phase 1 — Interface Failures
The world learns that ships are not the real bottleneck. Interfaces are.

A port cyberattack halts a region.
A customs database wipe makes legal cargo indistinguishable from contraband.
A cable landing fire blinds insurers and ports.
A sanctions dispute strands medicine and food.
A mined strait turns routing into warfare.
Orbital relay outages break container authentication.
A climate disaster creates humanitarian corridors that states cannot administer quickly.

Phase 2 — Emergency Continuity Compacts
States and insurers create temporary mechanisms to keep trade moving through war, sanctions, climate shocks, pandemics, cable cuts, orbital disruptions, and customs collapse.
Port operators, customs-tech vendors, freight platforms, cable landing operators, satellite networks, marine insurers, free-zone authorities, and humanitarian logistics contractors are folded into continuity compacts.
Phase 3 — Janus Consolidation
Janus becomes the private-public threshold operator for the global economy.
It controls:

port operating systems;
berth priority;
bonded warehouses;
customs ledgers;
cargo identity;
sanctions routing;
cable landing exchanges;
orbital relay partitions;
drone corridors;
emergency green lanes;
humanitarian exception status;
continuity security;
trade-risk markets.

Phase 4 — Great Person Recognition
By 2052, shutting Janus down would strand:

food and fertilizer;
organs and medicine;
refugee corridors;
port labor;
customs records;
cable repairs;
orbital relays;
military deconfliction;
disaster aid;
sanctioned-but-humanitarian cargo;
industrial spare parts;
coastal and island city imports.

That makes Janus a plausible Great Corporate Person.
Recommended Name: Janus Continuity Group
Why It Works
Janus is the Roman god of gates, thresholds, roads, beginnings, endings, passages, and transitions. This maps almost too perfectly onto:

port gates;
customs gates;
cable gateways;
orbital gates;
launch windows;
bonded corridors;
refugee thresholds;
cargo identity changes;
legal exceptions.

The double-face symbolism also fits the setting: one face is humanitarian continuity, the other is quiet interdiction and toll extraction.
Possible issue: Janus is somewhat familiar/mythic. If this feels too stylized, use Gatehouse Continuity Authority for a drier bureaucratic version.
Common names:

Janus
JCG
The Gate
The Second Customs
The Company That Says Yes
Saint Janus
the Red Light
No-Scan

Name Options
1. Janus Continuity Group
Best current recommendation.
Pros: strong threshold symbolism, broad enough for ports/cables/orbit/customs, memorable, fits public/dark duality.
Cons: mythic; may need sober subsidiaries to ground it.
2. Gatehouse Continuity Authority
Pros: dry, quasi-sovereign, very clear. Good if Janus feels too mythic.
Cons: less brandable and more governmental.
3. Portcullis Global
Pros: gate/defense symbolism, old-world border feel, distinctive.
Cons: too obviously restrictive; less plausible as benevolent public brand.
4. Atlas Gateworks
Pros: global, load-bearing, industrial.
Cons: Atlas is overused; “Gateworks” slightly stylized.
5. Kestrel Transit Authority
Pros: movement, speed, surveillance, skies.
Cons: sounds too aviation/transit and not enough customs/cargo.
6. Straitline Global
Pros: maritime chokepoints, efficiency, trade lanes.
Cons: too ocean-specific; weaker for orbit/data/customs.
7. Keelnet Continuity
Pros: nice ship/network hybrid.
Cons: too startup-ish; too ship-centered.
8. Harborline Relay Trust
Pros: sober, plausible, legal trust feel.
Cons: too harbor-specific.
9. Peregrine Gateways
Pros: movement/migration feel, elegant.
Cons: too premium travel/aviation.
10. BlueGate Continuity Group
Earlier strong option.
Pros: clear, global, sea/sky/network/gate meaning.
Cons: “Blue” risks generic tech/humanitarian branding; Janus is more distinctive.
11. Asterion Passage Authority
Pros: quasi-sovereign, strong passage control, more mythic.
Cons: more fictional/fantasy tone; less corporate realism.
12. Chokepoint Continuity Corporation
Pros: brutally accurate.
Cons: no real public-facing corporation would call itself this. Use as activist nickname.
Corporate Hierarchy
JanusPorts
Terminal software, automated cranes, berthing auctions, drone tug lanes, port cybersecurity, labor credentialing, continuity-zone enforcement.
Public face: ports that never stop.
Dark face: port cities become corporate borderlands.
JanusCustoms
Bonded-cargo ledgers, tariff classification, sanctions compliance, export-control logic, dual-use scoring, trusted consignment status.
Public face: efficient, rules-based clearance.
Dark face: the world’s largest switchboard for selective smuggling and algorithmic embargo.
GateLedger
Cargo identity and provenance network. It does for goods what Axiom does for persons and civil records.
Public face: anti-fraud cargo truth.
Dark face: if GateLedger suspends a container, it becomes commercially unreal.
RelayJanus
Orbital relay, ground-station, maritime satellite backup, port-to-orbit communication, orbital drop coordination, emergency store-and-forward.
Public face: resilient communications.
Dark face: bandwidth priority as political obedience.
BlueSplice
Cable landing stations, cable repair logistics, wet-plant monitoring, exchange routing, emergency bandwidth rationing.
Public face: repair the broken internet.
Dark face: restore one city in 36 hours and leave another dark for three weeks.
Boundary: BlueSplice does not certify polar cable corridors; that remains Barents’ lane. BlueSplice operates landings, exchanges, and repair logistics in the global system.
Bondline
Extraterritorial bonded corridors: fenced rail, drone highways, customs-neutral ports, warehouse cities, floating jurisdiction barges.
Public face: trade continuity.
Dark face: legal limbo and corridor sovereignty.
Continuity Desk
Crisis-routing bureau activated during war, famine, epidemic, flood, coup, sanctions shock, orbital debris cascade, port strike, or cable cut.
Public face: emergency response.
Dark face: decides who receives exception status.
Red Seal Risk
Private inspection, enforcement, interdiction, customs security, drone suppression, port riot control, cable landing protection.
Public face: safe trade.
Dark face: private border police in customs colors.
Saint Elmo Exchange
Berth futures, cold-chain options, cable repair priority markets, corridor insurance, war-risk pricing, continuity bonds.
Public face: finance for resilience.
Dark face: disaster speculation.
Geography
Core Headquarters
Singapore — operational HQ, maritime arbitration, Malacca/South China Sea relevance, port authority legitimacy.
Rotterdam / The Hague — port systems, treaty law, arbitration, EU customs integration.
Dubai / Jebel Ali — free-zone administration, Gulf capital, Africa-Asia-Europe routing.
Panama City / Colón — canal continuity and Americas customs corridors.
This multi-seat structure is more believable than a single global capital. Janus is literally a threshold firm; its headquarters are also thresholds.
Major Nodes
Singapore / Malacca — global chokepoint, Asian routing, relay control.
Rotterdam / Antwerp — European gateway and inland corridor.
Jebel Ali / Dubai / Abu Dhabi — capital, free zones, Indian Ocean routing.
Suez / Port Said / Ain Sokhna — canal redundancy and Red Sea crisis routing.
Tangier Med / Casablanca — Atlantic-Med gateway.
Mombasa / Lamu / Djibouti — East African humanitarian and military logistics.
Colombo / Hambantota / Chennai / Mumbai — Indian Ocean interface.
Busan / Yokohama / Kaohsiung — Northeast Asian manufacturing and orbital relay ties.
Los Angeles / Long Beach / Vancouver / Prince Rupert — Pacific North American gateways.
Santos / Fortaleza / Recife — South Atlantic cables and Brazil-Africa cargo.
Lagos / Lekki / Cape Town / Durban — African port growth and bonded corridors.
Tallinn / Helsinki / Gdansk — Baltic/EU continuity interfaces, with Axiom and Tryzub adjacency.
Darwin / Perth — Indo-Pacific contingency and orbital ground-station access.
Orbital / Relay Footprint

equatorial ground stations in Kenya, Singapore, Brazil, Ecuador, Indonesia, and Gulf states;
high-latitude backup stations leased from Barents-certified facilities;
LEO relay partitions licensed through state coalitions;
maritime store-and-forward channels;
emergency “deadman bandwidth” for ports, hospitals, food corridors, and military deconfliction.

Public Face
Janus says it:

keeps medicine, food, energy, and repair parts moving when borders fail;
harmonizes customs without abolishing sovereignty;
fights smuggling and forced labor;
protects cable landings and port systems;
coordinates humanitarian corridors;
restores emergency bandwidth;
keeps islands and coastal cities alive after storms;
prevents sanctions from blocking legitimate relief;
reduces war-risk uncertainty;
makes autonomous trade legally accountable.

Some of this is true.
Janus is frightening because it can be the only reason relief arrives.
Dark Face
Janus does not merely move things. It defines reality at the border.
It can:

downgrade a district’s lane priority;
suspend cargo identity;
make a port uninsurable;
deny humanitarian exception status;
delay cable repair;
sell premium bandwidth during crisis;
reclassify medicine as dual-use;
move protected cargo through sealed continuity channels;
strand refugees in bonded limbo;
make sanctions laundering look lawful;
turn disaster corridors into permanent concessions;
decide which smuggling is criminal and which is “exceptional.”

Its greatest weapon is not a fleet or an army.
It is the clearance code.
Relationships With Existing Great Persons
QXZ Meridian
QXZ Meridian prices climate risk and adaptation. Janus operationalizes climate reality through ports, routes, and continuity certification.
Conflict: QXZ may declare a coastal port unadaptable; Janus may keep it alive because it is a strategic gate. Or Janus may withdraw port continuity before QXZ officially declares the city doomed, causing self-fulfilling collapse.
Tryzub Systems
Tryzub Systems secures war and resilience systems. Janus controls the civilian-military logistics threshold.
Conflict: Tryzub wants speed and necessity. Janus wants legal legibility and toll control. Tryzub can move force; Janus can deny supply without firing.
Barents Research Group
Barents Research Group certifies polar routes, Arctic cables, mineral claims, and frontier infrastructure. Janus decides whether that certified route or cargo can circulate globally.
Conflict: Barents can say a polar route is open. Janus can say the cargo has no recognized customs state.
Helvetia
Helvetia certifies lawful cognition for autonomous ports, customs classifiers, berth-recognition AIs, orbital relays, and cargo adjudication.
Conflict: Helvetia may rule a Janus customs AI unlawful. Janus may claim continuity emergency privilege.
Axiom
Axiom makes persons and records legible. Janus makes cargo, routes, and logistics permissions legible.
Cooperation: organ shipments, refugee records, sanctions lists, evidence chain-of-custody, disaster relocation.
Conflict: Axiom may say a person exists and has rights. Janus may still say they lack corridor status.
Dark convergence:

When Axiom and Janus agree, a person can move through the world. When either says no, they are trapped. When both erase you, you were never there.

Verdant
Verdant coordinates food, nutrients, seed stock, famine response, and feedability. Janus moves it through ports, cold chains, customs corridors, and emergency lanes.
Conflict: Verdant says a shipment prevents famine. Janus says it lacks lawful corridor status. Or Janus agrees to move it only through bonded depots at emergency rates.
Street-Level Consequences

Dockworkers, customs runners, drone wranglers, cable divers, tug pilots, and salvage crews live or die by Janus clearance.
A neighborhood can be green-laned for food and medicine or quietly deprioritized.
Smuggling becomes bureaucratic: the best smugglers corrupt cargo ontology instead of avoiding scanners.
Port cities contain Janus-administered continuity zones with private labor courts and blackout rules.
Refugees and fugitives can move as protected cargo or vanish into bonded legal limbo.
Cable repair crews have quasi-diplomatic status and armed escorts.
Black-market “red seals” are more valuable than guns.
A single cargo flag can change a shipment from medicine to contraband to humanitarian exception.

Game / Story Hooks

A Verdant famine shipment is trapped in Janus audit while riots begin.
A BlueSplice repair ship is installing a tap while “repairing” a cable.
A port AI flags the player’s cargo as dual-use; the flag was planted by a rival corp.
A refugee ferry is classified as bonded cargo to bypass Axiom review.
A dockworker strike becomes a citywide starvation timer.
A Tryzub convoy cannot cross a Janus-certified humanitarian gate.
A Barents polar shipment reaches port but lacks customs identity.
A Janus red seal is stolen and every faction wants it.
A Continuity Desk disaster corridor becomes a permanent corporate concession.
A Helvetia tribunal must decide whether a customs AI killed people by delay.

Comparative Alternative: Energy / Grid
Energy/grid is the strongest challenger to Janus for the eighth slot.
It would give:

blackouts;
cooling rationing;
grid sovereignty;
microreactor politics;
compute-power conflict;
desalination dependence;
battery/mineral pressure;
urban survival stakes.

Possible names:

Blackstart Grid
Solenne Power
Voltaic Commons
GridSaint
Ashlight Energy
HelioDyne Authority
Nadir Gridworks

Why Janus still wins for now:

Helvetia already covers compute custody and therefore part of energy priority.
QXZ already covers climate adaptation and infrastructure risk.
Barents already covers extraction/minerals.
Energy is foundational but risks becoming “the infrastructure corp.”
Janus gives more distinctive movement, smuggling, ports, customs, orbit, and campaign-map pressure.

If later the setting feels weak on blackouts, cooling, and urban grid politics, create a major regional energy corporation or state-grid bloc rather than necessarily replacing Janus.
Recommendation
Develop Janus Continuity Group if the user accepts the slot.
Use Gatehouse Continuity Authority as the strongest drier alternative if Janus feels too mythic.
Use BlueGate Continuity Group only if a more humanitarian/sea-sky-network brand is preferred.
Do not make Janus a shipping company. Make it the private-public threshold layer that decides what can move, when, under what seal, under which exception, and at what price.

raw/brainstorms/unp-agi-compact-and-mega.title: UNP, AGI Compact, and Megacorp Order Brainstorm
raw/brainstorms/unp-agi-compact-and-mega.content:
UNP, AGI Compact, and Megacorp Order Brainstorm
Short Recommendation
The idea is strong, but it should not become a clean corporate world government.
The best Neon Champions version is:

After climate, war, AI, and infrastructure crises make the old UN visibly inadequate, states create the United Nations and Persons as a legitimacy and crisis-management forum. The UNP recognizes a tiny class of Great Corporate Persons because they control infrastructure that can destroy or sustain civilization. In exchange, these corporations accept AGI limits, inspection, climate duties, disclosure rituals, and formal crisis obligations. The arrangement prevents direct apocalypse while making lower-level proxy conflict, concession war, and corporate coercion normal.

This preserves the user’s goal:

AGI/ASI are out of bounds by compact, not just genre fiat.
Megacorps are internationally recognized, but not as cartoon sovereigns.
The UNP matters without becoming a world government.
Regional blocs, alliances, concessions, and local conflicts remain the real flow of power.
Great-power MAD logic pushes conflict downward into proxy wars and low-intensity violence.

Pushback
Do not make the megacorps simply equal to nations in every respect.
That is the weak version. It makes states look foolish and corporations look like fantasy kingdoms with logos.
The stronger version is legal asymmetry:

states remain sovereign;
megacorps are recognized as persons, not nations;
their seats exist because they are systemically dangerous, not morally legitimate;
their voting powers are limited by subject matter;
they are bound by inspection, disclosure, emergency continuity duties, sanctions obligations, and liability arbitration;
everyone argues about whether recognition was necessary realism or formalized corporate feudalism.

The public should not agree that the arrangement is good. Many people should call it surrender.
What Replaced the Old UN
The old UN likely does not vanish overnight. It becomes inadequate through a sequence:

Security Council paralysis during climate emergency, Baltic War aftermath, AI threshold scares, and White Sky disputes.
States create side compacts for climate continuity, compute governance, frontier AI inspections, cable security, and emergency food logistics.
These side compacts increasingly include the corporations that actually operate the relevant systems.
The old UN becomes ceremonial, humanitarian, or legally inherited.
A post-crisis charter consolidates the side compacts into the United Nations and Persons.

The UNP name should sound aspirational and legalistic, not cute. “Persons” has multiple meanings:

natural persons: citizens/humans whose rights the charter claims to protect;
juridical persons: corporations and foundations;
collective persons: city compacts, indigenous authorities, labor federations, universities, recognized polities;
contested future persons: Echo estates, continuity shells, or synthetic-person claims that the charter carefully avoids resolving.

This gives the name bite: the institution is built around a fight over who counts.
The New Charter
The UNP Charter should contain high ideals and ugly compromises.
Likely pillars:


Artificial General Intelligence and Superintelligence Nonproliferation

No unsupervised AGI/ASI development, deployment, possession, transfer, or self-improvement.
Frontier compute and capability thresholds require declaration, licensing, evals, audits, and inspection.
Safe virtual intelligence remains legal and broadly available.



Climate Continuity and Anti-Termination Duties

White Sky maintenance cannot be abruptly abandoned.
Major climate infrastructure must be declared, insured, inspected, and operated under continuity plans.
Deliberate climate-maintenance collapse is treated as a crime against persons.



Prohibition on Large-Scale Territorial War

Formal conquest and mass annexation are charter violations.
This does not stop corridor wars, private-security conflicts, proxy wars, legal coercion, debt receiverships, or sabotage.



Continuity of Persons

Human survival, identity records, civil registries, bodies, medical access, and evacuation rights are charter language.
In practice, access depends on documentation, feed provenance, insurance, and platform identity.



Systemic Infrastructure Duties

Recognized Great Persons must maintain declared infrastructure: compute, climate, food, medical, logistics, security, identity, communications, and data custody.
Failure can trigger receivership, sanctions, inspection, or emergency operating authority.



Security Council Equivalent
The UNP should have a council, but it should not be a simple copy of the UN Security Council.
Candidate name: Continuity Council.
Composition idea:

major state seats: US/North Atlantic, China, India, European Union / European Security Compact, African Union or rotating African compact, possibly Brazil/Latin American seat, and others depending on final map;
Great Corporate Person seats: up to eight systemically recognized megacorps;
rotating regional seats;
non-voting or limited-vote chambers for labor, cities, indigenous authorities, scientific panels, and civil society;
a technical inspection directorate with unusual independence.

The council does not govern the world. It does four things:

defines threshold violations;
authorizes inspections and sanctions;
coordinates crisis de-escalation;
decides what counts as protected continuity infrastructure.

That last power is where the horror lives.
The Eight Great Corporate Persons
Eight is a good number for the setting: small enough to feel mythic and legible, large enough to support multiple factions and rivalries.
But all eight should not be equal in tone or product category. They should be recognized because each controls a continuity layer.
Current accepted / strong candidates:

QXZ Meridian — atmosphere, adaptation biotech, climate-risk insurance, food continuity, White Sky maintenance.
Tryzub Systems — war operating systems, drones, civil-defense continuity, battlefield verification, private-security command layers.
Barents Research Group — Arctic routes, polar data, extraction certification, undersea cables, cold compute, rescue/security.

Possible remaining continuity-layer slots:

Compute / Model Custody Megacorp — certified frontier compute, model-weight escrow, datacenter sovereignty, safe VI access.
Body / Health Continuity Megacorp — organs, prosthetics, subscriptions, fertility, pandemic defense, worker adaptation.
Food / Nutrient / Seed Logistics Megacorp — grain, fertilizer, seed DRM, fermentation protein, urban nutrient recovery, famine prevention.
Identity / Feed Provenance Megacorp — platform identity, verified feeds, civil registries, election evidence, Echo legality, synthetic-reality certification.
Ports / Cables / Orbital Logistics Megacorp — global shipping, customs tech, cable repair fleets, orbital relays, launch windows, sanctions-routing.

Some current candidates may merge or split. For example, QXZ already touches body and food continuity, so the roster should avoid redundant categories.
What the Compact Actually Prevents
The compact mostly prevents:

open AGI/ASI race by the biggest actors;
acknowledged state-corporate total war;
mass territorial conquest by great powers;
abrupt White Sky shutdown;
open destruction of core compute, food, body, or climate infrastructure.

It does not prevent:

proxy wars;
concession wars;
private-security massacres;
cyber sabotage;
chip smuggling;
illegal training runs;
synthetic insurgencies;
assassination of researchers;
feed manipulation;
selective humanitarian abandonment;
small-state coercion;
corporate receiverships;
deniable Champion operations.

This is the stability-instability paradox translated into Neon Champions.
Why Small Conflicts Increase
The largest actors cannot safely fight directly, so they push violence into spaces where responsibility can be denied:

unrecognized labs;
Free-Net zones;
sacrificed territories;
debt-receivership cities;
border corridors;
Arctic concessions;
West African rainfall claims;
cable chokepoints;
body-mineral extraction routes;
model freeports;
private security mandates.

Smaller powers become weaker in general but sometimes gain extraordinary leverage by holding a chokepoint. A small polity with a lithium corridor, cable landing, cooling-water basin, Meridian Station, rare archive, or chip-fab tool can become impossible to ignore.
How This Fits Existing Neon Champions Lore
White Sky
The White Sky becomes one of the charter’s founding traumas. The UNP does not undo it. It normalizes and regulates it.
QXZ can claim: without recognized corporate persons, there would be no accountable party to maintain planetary cooling.
Opponents claim: the UNP legalized hostage-taking after the hostage system was already built.
Virtual Intelligence
The virtual-intelligence-and-compute-scarcity compact becomes formalized. VI remains everywhere, but the charter forbids crossing into unsupervised AGI/ASI.
The line between VI and AGI stays contested because every actor has incentives to define it differently.
Champions
Champions become useful under the compact precisely because open apocalypse tools are prohibited. They are deniable, symbolic, human-facing instruments of limited war.
A Champion can be a living flag, proxy general, propaganda saint, crisis negotiator, corporate asset, or treaty violation disguised as a person.
Echoes
The word “Persons” creates legal pressure around echo-identity-and-death. The charter may deny Echo personhood publicly while quietly allowing Echo estates, continuity shells, memorial rights, and data-custody claims.
This is fertile conflict: humans, corporations, and Echo-adjacent entities all try to use the same legal language.
Strong In-World Phrases

“The Charter did not end war. It licensed the altitude at which war may breathe.”
“No AGI, no blue sky, no annexations. Everything else is negotiable.”
“Persons means whoever can survive arbitration.”
“The Continuity Council protects humanity from extinction and incumbents from obsolescence. Usually in that order. Usually.”
“The old UN asked states not to destroy each other. The UNP asks the machines that keep us alive not to leave.”

Key Open Questions

Is the formal name United Nations and Persons, or is that the common name for a longer legal title?
Are the Great Corporate Persons named in the charter, or certified through renewable recognition?
Do corporate seats vote on sanctions and inspections, or only on infrastructure continuity questions?
Which states opposed corporate seats and lost?
Which Global South or labor concessions made the charter politically survivable?
Did QXZ receive recognition before or after the first White Sky move?
Was Tryzub recognized because of the Baltic War, or later because everyone needed its survival doctrine?
Is any recognized Person secretly close to crossing the AGI threshold?

raw/references/albedo-modification-resea.title: Albedo Modification Research Background
raw/references/albedo-modification-resea.content:
Albedo Modification Research Background
Purpose
This is the consolidated reference page for the real-world science behind the white-sky. It is meant to be easy to find and use. The older source extraction page, national-academies-albedo-modification-chapter-2, remains as a narrower raw note.
This page is not canon prose. Use it to constrain canon pages, faction arguments, and map design.
Plain Summary
Albedo modification / solar radiation modification means deliberately reflecting or scattering more sunlight back into space so Earth absorbs less solar energy.
It can lower temperatures faster than CO2 removal, but it does not remove greenhouse gases. It does not directly reverse ocean acidification, restore ecosystems, undo committed sea-level rise, or recreate the old climate.
The core Neon Champions interpretation remains:

Humanity partially solved climate change by turning the sky into maintained, proprietary, politically contested life-support infrastructure.

Main Real-World Approaches
Stratospheric Aerosol Injection
Reflective particles or their chemical precursors are introduced into the stratosphere. Volcanic eruptions such as Pinatubo are often used as natural analogues because they produced temporary global cooling through stratospheric aerosols.
For Neon Champions this is the best basis for the visible pale sky: a maintained high-altitude veil that makes noon look white, surgical, and wrong.
Marine Cloud Brightening
Sea-salt or other particles are introduced near low marine clouds to make them brighter and more reflective.
For Neon Champions this supports cloud-brightening fleets, ocean maintenance corridors, coastal weather disputes, and accusations that one region’s rain was sacrificed for another’s cooling.
Surface Albedo / Regional Brightening
Reflective roofs, roads, salt flats, managed agricultural surfaces, and other brightened surfaces can alter local or regional heat absorption.
For Neon Champions this supports corporate heat-safe districts, white infrastructure, reflective corridors, and visual class markers.
Orbital or High-Altitude Reflectors
More speculative but useful as a later or elite layer: orbital mirrors, high-altitude platforms, or reflective swarms that assist monitoring or regional tuning.
Use carefully. This can become too space-opera if made dominant.
What It Can Do

Reduce global mean temperature relatively quickly.
Reduce some heat extremes.
Reduce cooling demand in some regions.
Buy time for adaptation or decarbonization.
Create measurable near-term benefits that make reversal politically difficult.

What It Cannot Do

Remove CO2.
Stop ocean acidification.
Restore extinct species, damaged reefs, degraded soils, or old weather patterns.
End sea-level rise already committed by past warming.
Guarantee fair regional rainfall.
Eliminate climate migration, food insecurity, or adaptation inequality.
Safely stop itself while greenhouse gas concentrations remain high.

Major Risks Useful for Fiction
Termination Shock
If a maintained albedo intervention stops abruptly while greenhouse gases remain high, warming can rebound rapidly. This gives White Sky operators enormous leverage: even opponents may fear shutting it down.
Regional Unevenness
A global cooling average can hide regional harm. Some areas may get less rainfall, delayed monsoons, lower solar yield, crop stress, or ecosystem disruption while others benefit.
This is crucial: White Sky can save millions from heat while still being a political crime against specific regions.
Rainfall and Monsoon Attribution
It may be hard to prove whether a drought, flood, late monsoon, or crop failure was caused by White Sky tuning, greenhouse warming, natural variability, local land use, or bad water governance.
That uncertainty is narratively valuable. Corporations can deny liability; harmed communities can organize around probabilistic injustice.
Governance and Consent
The technology could potentially be deployed by a single powerful state, corporation, coalition, or wealthy actor before global consensus. That makes unilateral first deployment plausible for Neon Champions.
Millennial Dependence
CO2 lasts far longer than aerosol/cloud interventions. A society can become dependent on continuous maintenance for generations.
Africa / Lower-Income Region Implications
Africa should not be written as simply anti-White-Sky. The stronger version is divided.
Some African city governments, health ministries, and workers may support White Sky because lower heat saves lives and reduces cooling demand.
Farmers, pastoralists, basin authorities, solar utilities, coastal communities, and climate-justice movements may oppose it because rainfall timing, river flows, solar yield, sea-level risk, and compensation are unequal.
Scientifically plausible pressure points:

West African monsoon timing and regional rainfall shifts.
Sahel heat, drought/flood volatility, grazing corridors, and farmer-pastoralist stress.
Horn of Africa drought/flood whiplash and displacement.
Lake Chad’s pulsing hydrology and contested water governance.
Nile Basin dam politics and rainfall attribution.
Congo Basin carbon, peatlands, biodiversity, forest loss, and bioprospecting.
Coastal West Africa, especially Lagos and Gulf of Guinea flood/heat/settlement pressure.
Southern Africa drought and hydropower volatility, especially Zambezi-linked power systems.
Mineral corridors where climate relief, debt, compute, and resource concessions are bundled.

Sources / Starting Points

National Academies 2015, Climate Intervention: Reflecting Sunlight to Cool Earth: www.nationalacademies.org/read/18988/chapter/4
National Academies 2021, Reflecting Sunlight: www.nationalacademies.org/read/25762/chapter/1
IPCC AR6 WG1: www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg1/
IPCC AR6 Africa fact sheet: www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg1/downloads/factsheets/IPCC_AR6_WGI_Regional_Fact_Sheet_Africa.pdf
IPCC AR6 WG2 Chapter 9, Africa: www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg2/chapter/chapter-9/
UNEP, One Atmosphere: www.unep.org/resources/report/Solar-Radiation-Modification-research-deployment
Harding et al. 2020 on solar geoengineering and income inequality: pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6957473/
Degrees Initiative summary on stratospheric sulfate aerosols and West African monsoon precipitation: degrees.ngo/research/stratospheric-sulfate-aerosols-impacts-on-west-african-monsoon-precipitation-using-geomip-models/

raw/references/greenland-strategic-setti.title: Greenland Strategic Setting Research 2026-05-22
raw/references/greenland-strategic-setti.content:
Greenland Strategic Setting Research 2026-05-22
Use for Neon Champions
Greenland is strong as the initial Neon Champions campaign region if treated as a sparse, high-value Arctic systems map: climate instability, mineral intrigue, sovereignty politics, strategic routes, isolated outposts, sensor infrastructure, and public legitimacy conflict.
The key correction is that climate change does not turn Greenland into a simple fertile paradise. It makes Greenland more accessible, more unstable, more valuable, and more contested.
Climate Impacts

The Greenland Ice Sheet has lost mass every year since 1998; ice loss changes sea level, fjords, freshwater flows, iceberg hazards, coastlines, and global politics.
Less sea ice can lengthen navigation windows, but also increases storm exposure, fog, wave damage, iceberg risk, coastal erosion, and insurance/security costs.
Permafrost thaw threatens foundations, roads, airstrips, pipelines, fuel depots, storage tanks, and waste sites.
Fisheries and marine ecosystems are likely more important than farmland as economic climate shifts.

Pushback: “New Green Land”
Greenland should not become a new Iowa or mass-grain frontier.
Constraints:

Greenland remains overwhelmingly ice sheet, mountain, rock, tundra, and permafrost.
Agriculture is realistic mainly in small southern ice-free areas; Britannica gives roughly one percent of land as agriculturally usable.
Soils are thin, rocky, immature, and drainage/permafrost problems remain severe.
The growing season expands but remains short and extremely seasonal.
Logistics, fuel, fertilizer, machinery, storage, and labor costs remain high.

Better Neon Champions translation:

“Green Zones” are corporate greenhouses, geothermal/hydro-powered vertical farms, algal vats, seed vaults, and PR-heavy adaptation agriculture projects.
Food security is tied to ports, cold storage, hydro power, fisheries, greenhouses, imported nutrients, and corporate concession terms.
The word “green” becomes political branding and a bitter local joke, not a literal breadbasket truth.

Strategic Resources
High-value resources and sites:

Fisheries: shrimp, halibut, cod, processing hubs, quota algorithms, cold storage.
Critical minerals: rare earths, zinc, lead, gold, iron, uranium-adjacent controversies, graphite, anorthosite, battery-chain claims.
Hydro power and cold climate: settlement-scale energy, compute-cooling claims, hydrogen projects.
Freshwater/ice: export myth, elite water brands, industrial cooling, symbolic control.
Data/space/weather infrastructure: satellite ground stations, radar, ice/weather routing, undersea sensors, Arctic cable routes, climate archives.
Legacy sites: old military installations, buried waste, abandoned mining camps, ice-core archives.

Geopolitics
Base reality:

Greenland is an autonomous territory in the Kingdom of Denmark.
Denmark retains major foreign-policy/defense responsibilities; Greenland governs most domestic affairs.
Independence is politically live but constrained by economic dependence and infrastructure needs.
Inuit/Greenlandic sovereignty, land consent, and cultural continuity must be central.

Plausible external actors:

Greenlandic government and municipal councils.
Denmark / Arctic Command.
United States, especially Pituffik/Thule-style space/security infrastructure.
EU critical-mineral and climate-adaptation finance.
China as mining/port/telecom investor and contested strategic partner.
Canada, Iceland, Norway, Arctic indigenous networks, insurers, logistics firms, mining corps, satellite firms, security contractors.
barents-research-group and qxz-meridian as in-world corporate powers.

Arctic Logistics

The strategic map should be a node-and-route map, not a road map.
Movement is by aircraft, helicopter, boat, snowmobile, dog sled, drone, seasonal ice road, or corporate convoy.
Sea lanes open and close by season, ice, insurance, weather data, and conflict.
More open Arctic water means more access and more danger, not easy shipping.

Settlement / Outpost Palette
Good hub analogues:

Nuuk: capital, government/corporate/security intrigue.
Sisimiut: fishery/education/industrial node.
Ilulissat: icefjord, tourism, fisheries, prestige science.
Qaqortoq / Narsaq: southern agriculture, mineral controversy, “green land” propaganda.
Aasiaat / Maniitsoq / Tasiilaq / Uummannaq / Qaanaaq: regional outposts, logistics, fisheries, remote politics.

Special strategic sites:

Pituffik Space Base / former Thule analogue: space, missile warning, orbital traffic, White Sky telemetry.
Kangerlussuaq: logistics choke point and air hub.
Summit Station: ice-sheet science and extreme survival.
Station Nord / Daneborg / Sirius patrol regions: sovereignty, wilderness, sensors.
Northeast Greenland National Park: remote patrol/research/wildlife zone.
Ilulissat Icefjord: prestige/UNESCO-like heritage and climate symbolism.

Cyberpunk Pressures

Critical-mineral rush disguised as green transition.
Climate finance colonialism: offsets, concessions, adaptation debt, glacier data rights.
Surveillance Arctic: radar, satellites, autonomous buoys, drone corridors.
Cold compute and hydro allocation conflict.
Fisheries algorithm wars and quota manipulation.
Civilian ports/airfields doubling as security architecture.
Indigenous data sovereignty disputes.
Legacy contamination from military/mining/research sites.
Insurance/security cartels deciding which routes and settlements are viable.
Climate-stressed animal sensor networks and weaponized wildlife experiments.

Wildlife / Mind-Control Hook
Mind-controlled or instrumented polar animals can work if grounded as:

telemetry collars and bioacoustic herding systems hacked into weapons;
defense neuro-interface experiments sold as wildlife management;
climate-stress disease/parasite research gone wrong;
animal sensor networks exploited by a faction;
polar bears, musk oxen, sled dogs, ravens, seals, narwhals, or whales as strategic warning/terror units.

Use sparingly. If overused, it becomes silly. The stronger version is “weaponized environmental management,” not fantasy beast mastery.
Recommended Design Translation
Greenland should supply:

wilderness vibe without fantasy wilderness;
outposts as town analogues;
mines, fishery hubs, data stations, White Sky nodes, and ports as strategic sites;
fragile logistics as movement economy;
legitimacy/consent as resource pressure;
Blue Week as public summit and hidden campaign crisis.

raw/references/national-academies-albedo.title: national-academies-albedo-modification-chapter-2
raw/references/national-academies-albedo.content:
National Academies: Climate Intervention by Modifying Earth’s Albedo
Source: www.nationalacademies.org/read/18988/chapter/4
Book: National Research Council. 2015. Climate Intervention: Reflecting Sunlight to Cool Earth. Washington, DC: The National Academies Press. doi: 10.17226/18988.
Chapter shown by the site: Chapter 2, “Climate Intervention by Modifying Earth’s Albedo”.
Relevant Scientific Takeaways for Neon Champions

The report prefers “albedo modification” over “solar radiation management” because it describes the physical process more neutrally: intentionally increasing the sunlight reflected/scattered back to space.
The two most discussed scalable approaches are stratospheric aerosol injection and marine cloud brightening.
Stratospheric aerosol injection means increasing small reflecting particles in the stratosphere, usually by injecting chemical precursors such as sulfur dioxide that later form aerosols.
Marine cloud brightening means adding substances near the ocean surface to make low clouds more reflective.
The core physics is top-of-atmosphere energy balance: greenhouse gases reduce outgoing infrared radiation; increased albedo reduces incoming absorbed solar radiation.
Rough scale: doubling preindustrial CO2 produces about 4 W/m² radiative forcing; reflecting about 2% of currently absorbed sunlight could offset that top-of-atmosphere imbalance.
The 1991 Pinatubo eruption is a natural analogue: it produced about -3 W/m² forcing shortly after eruption and cooled average surface air temperature about 0.3°C over roughly 3 years.
Albedo modification can reduce global mean temperature quickly, possibly within a few years, but it does not restore the preindustrial climate. It changes the mix of sunlight, regional temperatures, hydrology, plant conditions, and other Earth-system components.
It is not a substitute for decarbonization. If CO2 remains high, the intervention must be maintained; stopping it abruptly can trigger rapid warming.
The report calls this long-term dependency problem “millennial dependence risk”: aerosols or cloud effects dissipate in days to years, but CO2 forcing persists for millennia.
Large-scale deployment requires monitoring infrastructure: models of the injection protocol, observation of aerosol/albedo changes, and detection of climate response.
The report notes that as a matter of physical/economic capability, a single nation, a large corporation, or a group of wealthy actors could potentially deploy albedo modification without international consensus.
Many of the hardest risks are sociopolitical: governance, public opposition, liability, uneven harm, research/deployment incentives, and the possibility of unilateral action.

Neon Champions Use
White Sky should feel scientifically adjacent to albedo modification rather than generic “climate magic”: it cools Earth by reducing absorbed sunlight, but does not solve CO2, ocean chemistry, ecological stress, inequality, or governance. The strongest setting version is a corporate-led unilateral or semi-unilateral deployment that becomes too useful and too dangerous to stop.

raw/references/net-governance-reference-.content:
Net Governance Reference Research 2026-05-22
Core Recommendation
A UNP-coordinated Net is strong if it is a contested public substrate, not a clean world-government internet.
Use this model:

UNP coordinates the spine.
Great Corporate Persons own luxury/private arteries.
Cities and states run local organs.
Activists, criminals, refugees, smugglers, and cults tunnel through the nerves.
Rogue systems and old infrastructure haunt the scar tissue.

Fictional Analogues
Cyberpunk NetWatch
Useful pattern:

International/semi-international cyber police.
Protects the Net, pursues netrunners, contains catastrophic threats.
Can be ally, antagonist, or necessary evil.

Pushback:

Do not make the Neon Champions equivalent omnipotent.
Jurisdictional gaps, private layers, corruption, corporate pressure, blind spots, and old ruins must remain.

Shadowrun Matrix / GOD
Useful pattern:

Segmented grids: public, local, corporate, government, premium.
Overwatch-style escalating trace pressure.

Neon Champions translation:

Fragment heat by jurisdiction: UNP Heat, Corporate Heat, Civic Heat, Ghost Heat.
Do not make one universal all-seeing detection score.

IC / Black ICE
Useful treaty categories:

White IC: authentication, sandboxing, logging, throttling.
Gray IC: active tracing, deception, temporary lockout, compute seizure.
Red IC: destructive counter-intrusion for critical infrastructure / AGI quarantine.
Black ICE: outlawed or war-crime-adjacent except under sealed mandate; corporations still deploy it illegally.

Real-World Analogues

ICANN: names/numbers coordination, not world police.
IETF: standards and protocols by multi-stakeholder process.
ITU / UN cyber efforts: capacity-building, norms, telecom/cyber coordination.
UN peacekeeping: consent, impartiality, mandate limits, minimum force.
Tor / .onion: hidden-service namespaces outside ordinary DNS resolution.
ARPANET / mesh / pirate radio: networks emerge where central infrastructure is absent, censored, distrusted, or unaffordable.

Neon Champions Four-Layer Net Ecology
1. Treaty Net / Civic Net
UNP-coordinated public substrate: identity, civic services, emergency access, baseline communication, public archives, humanitarian infrastructure, cross-border routing, AGI Compact chokepoints.
2. Corporate Sovereign Grids
Great Corporate Person layers: faster, cleaner, safer, more immersive, paid, proprietary, exploitative, loyalty-scored, protected by private IC, connected by treaty gateways.
3. Free-Net / Polluted Digital-Net
Mass public feed ecology: cheap access, ad saturation, misinformation, bot swarms, abandoned platforms, compromised AR overlays, old data, low-grade VI sludge. Neglected, not fully lawless.
4. Dark / Pirate / Mesh Nets
Unregistered namespaces, onion-like routes, local mesh clouds, pirate AR overlays, smuggler relays, activist nodes, black clinics, illegal compute clusters, and emergency folk infrastructure.
UNP Net Security Body
Working-name candidates:

UNP Net Stabilization Authority
Digital Peacekeeping Directorate
BlueWatch
Net Peacekeeping Command
TreatyNet Authority
Mandate Blue

Mandate:

Defend critical civilian infrastructure.
Preserve minimum public access.
Prevent monopolistic capture of public routing/compute.
Enforce AGI Compact quarantines.
Coordinate cross-border cyber incident response.
Audit corporate treaty gateways.
Maintain emergency “blue lanes” for hospitals, courts, refugees, disaster systems, food systems, orbital traffic, and peacekeeping operations.

Limits:

It is treaty-based, mandate-bound, politically constrained, and dependent on states and corporations.
It is accused of overreach by corporations, surveillance colonialism by activists, weakness by hardliners, and hypocrisy by pirate nets.

Pushback to Centralization
If UNP can balance all compute/energy, police all layers, and prevent capture effectively, the setting loses cyberpunk tension. It should be important and sometimes heroic, but slow, infiltrated, underfunded, mandate-bound, politically compromised, and technically unable to see everything.
